source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Exact source records mapped to established public labels; mapping is recorded for every verse and verified against source KJV annotations. Daniel, Hosea, Joel, Jonah, Micah, and Nahum have chapter-boundary differences.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Preserves vision heading, plural we, divine titles, and the messenger's mobilizing words.
verses.before: The vision of Obadiah. Thus says the Lord GOD concerning Edom: We have heard a report from the LORD, and a messenger has been sent among the nations: “Rise up! Let us rise against her for battle!”
verses.after: The vision of Obadiah. This is what the Lord GOD says concerning Edom: We have heard a report from the LORD; a messenger has been sent among the nations: “Rise! Let us rise against her for battle!”
verses.tsw_comparator: The vision of Obadiah. Thus says the Lord GOD concerning Edom: We have heard a report from the LORD, and a messenger has been sent among the nations: “Rise up! Let us rise against her for battle!”

verses.rationale: Retains completed-form abasement and the direct address to Edom.
verses.before: Look, I have made you small among the nations; you are greatly despised.
verses.after: “Look, I have made you small among the nations; you are deeply despised.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I have made you small among the nations; you are greatly despised.

verses.rationale: Keeps heart repeated, rock/high dwelling, and the boast's downward challenge.
verses.before: The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, in your lofty dwelling, who say in your heart, “Who will bring me down to the ground?”
verses.after: The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who live in clefts of rock, whose dwelling is high, who say in your heart, ‘Who can bring me down to the ground?’
verses.tsw_comparator: The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, in your lofty dwelling, who say in your heart, “Who will bring me down to the ground?”

verses.rationale: Answers the boast through the same bring-down verb and cosmic nesting image.
verses.before: Though you soar high like the eagle, though your nest is set among the stars, from there I will bring you down, says the LORD.
verses.after: Even if you soar like an eagle and set your nest among the stars, I will bring you down from there,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though you soar high like the eagle, though your nest is set among the stars, from there I will bring you down, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the interrupted exclamation and the two comparisons with incomplete ordinary plunder.
verses.before: If thieves came to you, if robbers came by night— how you have been destroyed!— would they not steal only what they wanted? If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings?
verses.after: If thieves came to you, if robbers came by night— how utterly you have been destroyed!— would they not steal only enough for themselves? If grape pickers came to you, would they not leave gleanings?
verses.tsw_comparator: If thieves came to you, if robbers came by night— how you have been destroyed!— would they not steal only what they wanted? If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings?

verses.rationale: Preserves the Esau name and thorough searching rather than a vague loss of wealth.
verses.before: How Esau has been searched out! How his hidden treasures have been sought out!
verses.after: How Esau has been searched through, his hidden treasures hunted out!
verses.tsw_comparator: How Esau has been searched out! How his hidden treasures have been sought out!

verses.rationale: Makes the bread partners intelligible while preserving the final third-person shift and obscure trap term.
verses.before: All your allies have driven you to the border; those at peace with you have deceived you and prevailed against you. Those who eat your bread have set a trap beneath you. There is no understanding in him.
verses.after: All your allies have driven you to the border. Your trusted friends have deceived and overpowered you. Those who share your bread set a trap beneath you. There is no understanding in him.
verses.tsw_comparator: All your allies have driven you to the border; those at peace with you have deceived you and prevailed against you. Those who eat your bread have set a trap beneath you. There is no understanding in him.

verses.rationale: Keeps rhetorical question and parallel wise/understanding loss.
verses.before: On that day, says the LORD, will I not destroy the wise from Edom and understanding from Mount Esau?
verses.after: “On that day,” declares the LORD, “will I not destroy the wise from Edom and understanding from Esau’s mountain?
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day, says the LORD, will I not destroy the wise from Edom and understanding from Mount Esau?

verses.rationale: Preserves Teman address and explicit slaughter rather than mere military defeat.
verses.before: Your warriors will be terrified, O Teman, so that everyone from Mount Esau will be cut off by slaughter.
verses.after: Your warriors will be terrified, Teman, so that everyone on Esau’s mountain will be cut off in the slaughter.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your warriors will be terrified, O Teman, so that everyone from Mount Esau will be cut off by slaughter.

verses.rationale: Keeps fraternal relationship as the charge's force and repeated cut-off judgment.
verses.before: Because of violence against your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.
verses.after: Because of violence against your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of violence against your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated day, read plural gates, and complicity without claiming all violence was directly committed by Edom.
verses.before: On the day when you stood aloof, on the day when strangers carried away his wealth, when foreigners entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you were like one of them.
verses.after: On the day you stood aside, on the day strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the day when you stood aloof, on the day when strangers carried away his wealth, when foreigners entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you were like one of them.

verses.rationale: Keeps prohibitive form rather than silently changing to past should-not-have and preserves day refrain.
verses.before: Do not look with pleasure on the day of your brother, on the day of his misfortune. Do not rejoice over the children of Judah on the day of their destruction. Do not boast on the day of distress.
verses.after: Do not gloat over your brother’s day, the day of his calamity. Do not rejoice over Judah’s people on the day they perish; do not boast on the day of distress.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not look with pleasure on the day of your brother, on the day of his misfortune. Do not rejoice over the children of Judah on the day of their destruction. Do not boast on the day of distress.

verses.rationale: Retains the three repeated disaster clauses and possession shifts.
verses.before: Do not enter the gate of my people on the day of their disaster. Do not look with pleasure on their calamity on the day of their disaster. Do not reach for their wealth on the day of their disaster.
verses.after: Do not enter my people’s gate on the day of their disaster. Do not gloat over his suffering on the day of his disaster. Do not reach for his wealth on the day of his disaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not enter the gate of my people on the day of their disaster. Do not look with pleasure on their calamity on the day of their disaster. Do not reach for their wealth on the day of their disaster.

verses.rationale: Keeps interception and betrayal as separate actions against escapees.
verses.before: Do not stand at the crossroads to cut down those who escape. Do not hand over the survivors on the day of distress.
verses.after: Do not stand at the crossroads to cut down his fugitives; do not hand over his survivors on the day of distress.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not stand at the crossroads to cut down those who escape. Do not hand over the survivors on the day of distress.

verses.rationale: Preserves widening from Edom to nations and the head image of recompense.
verses.before: For the day of the LORD is near upon all the nations. As you have done, it will be done to you; your deeds will return upon your own head.
verses.after: For the day of the LORD is near for all the nations. As you have done, it will be done to you; your repayment will return upon your own head.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the day of the LORD is near upon all the nations. As you have done, it will be done to you; your deeds will return upon your own head.

verses.rationale: Keeps shift to plural you and the ambiguous drinking image, not specifying celebratory or judgment drink in text.
verses.before: For just as you drank on my holy mountain, so all the nations will drink continually. They will drink and swallow and become as though they had never been.
verses.after: Just as you drank on my holy mountain, all the nations will drink continually. They will drink and gulp down and become as though they had never been.
verses.tsw_comparator: For just as you drank on my holy mountain, so all the nations will drink continually. They will drink and swallow and become as though they had never been.

verses.rationale: Retains possession root repetition and holy mountain rather than modern territorial gloss.
verses.before: But on Mount Zion there will be those who escape, and it will be holy. The house of Jacob will possess its possessions.
verses.after: But on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be holy. The house of Jacob will possess its possessions.
verses.tsw_comparator: But on Mount Zion there will be those who escape, and it will be holy. The house of Jacob will possess its possessions.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three houses, destructive fire metaphor, and complete stated outcome.
verses.before: The house of Jacob will be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, but the house of Esau will be stubble. They will burn among them and consume them, and there will be no survivor of the house of Esau, for the LORD has spoken.
verses.after: The house of Jacob will be fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will burn through them and consume them; no survivor will remain of the house of Esau.” For the LORD has spoken.
verses.tsw_comparator: The house of Jacob will be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, but the house of Esau will be stubble. They will burn among them and consume them, and there will be no survivor of the house of Esau, for the LORD has spoken.

verses.rationale: Supplies people for regional subjects and retains every territorial pairing.
verses.before: Those of the Negev will possess Mount Esau, and those of the foothills the land of the Philistines. They will possess the territory of Ephraim and the territory of Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.
verses.after: The people of the Negev will possess Esau’s mountain, and the people of the foothills the Philistine country. They will possess the territory of Ephraim and Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those of the Negev will possess Mount Esau, and those of the foothills the land of the Philistines. They will possess the territory of Ephraim and the territory of Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.

verses.rationale: Uses company for obscure hel and supplies land to the elliptical possession clause; leaves Sepharad unidentified.
verses.before: The exiles of this host of the children of Israel will possess the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad will possess the cities of the Negev.
verses.after: The exiles of this company of Israelites will possess the Canaanites’ land as far as Zarephath, and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad will possess the cities of the Negev.
verses.tsw_comparator: The exiles of this host of the children of Israel will possess the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad will possess the cities of the Negev.

verses.rationale: Follows pointed active deliverers rather than rescued ones and preserves final divine kingship.
verses.before: Deliverers will go up to Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau, and the kingdom will belong to the LORD.
verses.after: Deliverers will go up on Mount Zion to judge Esau’s mountain, and the kingship will belong to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Deliverers will go up to Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau, and the kingdom will belong to the LORD.

comparative_references.scope: All 21 TSW verses bound and compared programmatically after independent drafting from each selected original-language record and all annotations. Selected differences read during focused authoring checks. Overlap is triage only.
